goal: Fold the long-sleeve shirt lying flat on the table: first fold both sleeves in across the chest, then fold the bottom hem up to the shoulders, using both arms, and finish with both arms back home with grippers open.
success: Garment geometry is read from tagged mesh vertices of the cloth 'target' (a long-sleeve top, category Top_Long): each tag (left_sleeve, right_sleeve, left_chest, right_chest, left_hem, right_hem, left_shoulder, right_shoulder) is the mean position of its tagged mesh vertices. Differences A-B are projected onto the garment's OWN local x axis and y axis (the root-orientation-rotated unit vectors, not fixed world axes), measured in metres. All range tests are strict (lower < diff < upper).

Sleeves folded in (both): left_sleeve minus right_chest has x-diff in (-0.125, 0.14) m and y-diff in (-0.125, 0.14) m; right_sleeve minus left_chest has x-diff in (-0.14, 0.125) m and y-diff in (-0.125, 0.14) m. (Each sleeve tip is brought to within about 13 to 14 cm of the opposite chest point.)

Bottom hem folded up to the shoulders (both sides): for side in {left,right}: {side}_hem minus {side}_shoulder has y-diff in (-0.095, 0.17) m and x-diff in (-0.12, 0.12) m (hem lies next to the shoulder).

Hem line direction vs shoulder line direction: the xy-projected vector left_hem->right_hem and the xy-projected vector left_shoulder->right_shoulder make an angle < 45 degrees (not folded sideways/flipped; vector direction matters, anti-parallel fails).

At the evaluation moment (see evaluation) all target grippers are open (opening fraction >= 0.7, normalised to the gripper scale) and all target arms are back at start pose (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m, rotation <= 20 degrees, all_robot_back_to_origin defaults); these are the trigger condition, not additional geometry.

Order constraint (failure rule, aim 0): at any moment a single arm becomes 'back at origin' (rising edge of is_robot_back_to_origin for left_arm, and separately for right_arm; same 0.15 m per axis/20 degree tolerance), if the garment is already hem-folded (hem/shoulder tests and the 45 degree line test all true) while at least one of the four sleeve closeness tests (left x, left y, right x, right y) is NOT satisfied, the episode is marked failed. I.e. the sleeves must be folded in before the bottom is folded up.
evaluation: Event-triggered, not checked every step. A trigger_check is registered with trigger condition C = (all target grippers open >= 0.7) AND (all robots back at origin), trigger mode rising_edge, evaluated after every action. The garment checks (both sleeves folded AND hem folded AND hem/shoulder line angle < 45 deg) are evaluated only on a step where C is true and was false on the previous step (initial previous value is false, so it is also evaluated once on the first step when the arms are home with open grippers; the flat garment fails it). If the garment checks pass at such an edge the check is removed and reward becomes 1: success. If they fail, nothing more is checked until C becomes false (e.g. an arm leaves home or a gripper closes below 0.7) and true again. So a folded garment with the arms already sitting at home since before the fold is not detected: the arms must leave and return to the home pose (with open grippers) after the garment is folded. Two additional trigger_queries (aim 0) run independently on the rising edges of left_arm-home and right_arm-home; if at such an edge the hem is folded while the sleeves are not all folded in, the episode fails immediately (success=False). Otherwise the episode fails at step_lim=500 actions. Process score (partial only) 20 for sleeves folded with grippers open, 100 for fully folded.
objects: target: long-sleeve top garment (category Top_Long, model index in {6, 7, 11}, 1 chosen per episode), cloth, laid flat on the table, x in [-0.02,0.02], y in [-0.25,-0.18] (m), random yaw within +/-25 degrees.

Clutter: 20 distractor objects (category_unique) scattered on the table x in [-0.6,0.6], y in [-0.5,0.5], yaw +/-30 deg, margin 0.015; keep-out area x[-0.35,0.35], y[-0.5,-0.4]. Not part of the reward.
needs_memory_or_language: none (fixed instruction; the required folding order is only implicit: sleeves first then hem).
end_requirements: At the moment the success check triggers: both grippers open (>= 0.7 of opening range) and both arms within 0.15 m per axis / 20 degrees of their start end-effector pose, reached via a rising edge (see evaluation).
notes: Dual-arm task (arm tags left_arm and right_arm must exist). Success is detected only at edges where both arms return home with open grippers, so the solver must explicitly (a) finish the folding, (b) open grippers, (c) return both arms to the home pose after the folding, having been away from home/gripper-closed before that step. Left/right labels (sleeve, chest, shoulder) are garment-side labels from asset metadata; which physical side they are cannot be determined statically. Distances are in the garment's local x/y axes, which rotate with the cloth's root orientation (a cloth root orientation that does not follow deformation could affect the measures; not determinable statically). Tolerances are fairly loose (about 12 to 17 cm) but the point sets are vertex means so a well flattened fold is needed. Compared with fold_clothes, this _random variant uses garment models 6, 7, 11 instead of 1, 4, 9 and adds clutter; the reward is identical.
